name: UJ-26 Beaver (Bober)

placement_rationale.text: 500 km is a confirmed/typical strike depth, not a launch-site offset — Beaver launches from inside Ukraine, so the crew/launch position sits far outside this figure. It lands at exactly half this asset's own sourced ~1,000 km range, the same conservative reading applied to Scythe (375 km against 750 km) rather than the nominal maximum, landing it at the top edge of the strategic_rear band (150–500 km) — appropriate for one of the earliest and longest-established members of Ukraine's deep-strike drone family, extending doctrine.md §2's 10–150+ km medium/long-range strike layer into strategic depth.

characteristics: Canard layout, sleek fuselage, inverted tail
Strength: Longer range than most contemporaries at the time of introduction; mass production gives sustained strike tempo rather than one-off attacks
Limitation: Payload (20kg) is modest compared to newer purpose-built strike types like FP-1/FP-2's 40kg warhead
Estimated quantity available: Reportedly in mass production; exact numbers not disclosed
employment_notes: One of the earliest Ukrainian deep-strike drones to repeatedly hit Moscow and other targets deep in Russia, establishing the template other domestic long-range types followed
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional deep-strike doctrine assumed reach came from a missile's range or a bomber's radius of action, and that targets hundreds of kilometres from the front were accordingly safe. A mass-producible one-way attack drone extends that reach for a fraction of a cruise missile's cost, the same collapse of the distance-equals-safety assumption doctrine.md notes for cross-border strike UAVs generally.
